correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 the Walsh-diagonalized cube Laplacian gives exact rational beta-integral expressions for each signed transfer-current entry. Positivity of all integrands fixes the sign pattern. The two basepoint columns on parallel square edges have signs equal in all directions except the shifted direction, where their entries are exact negatives; summing over edge bases gives direction-one mass 1 and each transverse mass 1/2. The deleted-graph inverse follows by Sherman–Morrison on the mean-zero vertex space since \(0<r_n<1\). These identities imply the exact witnessed cut gain \(d_n=(n-3)a_n/[2(1-r_n)]\) and cycle gain \(z_n=d_n-2a_n^2/(1-r_n)\). Both are strictly positive for all n>=4 using \(0<a_n<2/[n(n-1)]\). Exact rational grounded-Laplacian inversion checks all 124 remaining-edge columns in dimensions n=2,3,4,5 and exhausts the four edge classes for n=3; this is supplemental to the infinite proof. No unproved maximality in n>=4 is asserted.

value.rationale: The theorem isolates a natural sharp dimensional onset for norm amplification after a minimal graph perturbation: both complementary endpoint projections on cubes increase despite deleting an edge, for every dimension n>=4. It supplies explicit positive analytical lower-bound increments asymptotically 1/n, and proves complete smaller-dimensional exceptions. Such sensitivity of two Banach-space projection norms is not a restatement of a generic Sherman–Morrison update and gives a motivated boundary example for flow localization under graph modifications. The result requires no global exact post-deletion norm classification to have value.
